ingredients.item: scallions , finely sliced, whites and greens separated

instructions.heading: Raw build
instructions.action: Raw build: soy, vinegar, and honey stirred clear; scallions (all of them), gochugaru, sesame seeds, and the sesame oil folded in. Done, and better after ten minutes' rest while the scallion bleeds its green into the soy.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: the taste: salt first, vinegar's snap right behind, scallion's onion-sweetness, sesame's finish, the gochugaru coloring the whole thing warm. On a piece of fatty brisket shaving (#M07), the fat should taste cleaner after the dip, not greasier — that is the bowl's whole function.

instructions.heading: Bloomed build
instructions.action: Bloomed build: neutral oil and the garlic slices at medium-low until the garlic is blond; the scallion whites and gochugaru in for 30 seconds just to wake; pour the sizzling oil over the soy-vinegar-honey base with the scallion greens and sesame already in it. It crackles, blooms, and goes quiet.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: the bloomed bowl is rounder — the raw edge of vinegar and scallion cooked a half-step toward sweet — and it keeps a day longer. Both bowls should be assertive; a shy yangnyeom ganjang is soy sauce with regrets.

storageNotes: Raw build keeps 3 days (add the greens at serving); bloomed keeps 5. Both hold the flavors that make grilled meat interesting.
Variations: the onion-fork (#SA05); a pinch of black pepper for the beef records; a teaspoon of the gochujang (#SA03) swirled in for a bowl that leans hot — labeled as the hybrid it is.
